attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, presented as an example he wrote in a reply to Legg.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense claim about the state of driving AI at publication. The 'unusual circumstances' scope is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (a substantial gap on unusual road situations as of 2023) is ordinary and fair. Requiring matched comparisons is reasonable. The speaker gave no margin, scenario set or baseline, so the evaluator's interpretation decides the result.

evidence.note: Official SF filing from May 2023 lists AV failures at emergency and construction scenes. It has no human exposure baseline, so it cannot measure the gap.
Waymo's own 2022 simulation results on selected crash reconstructions. It is a company disclosure from before the target period with narrow scope.
Waymo-affiliated insurance-claims comparison with data to August 2023. Aggregate crash outcomes do not isolate unusual situations.

reviews.rationale: The incident records point to failures in unusual situations but give no human comparison. The Waymo simulations and claims data point the other way, but they are selected or aggregate measures. Nothing in the packet meets the contract's requirement for representative, matched comparisons of unusual driving, so the evidence settles neither the support nor the contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentences in his own post. The Nie et al quote nearby is separate and not part of this claim.

semantics.note: Reading 'them' as benchmarks is correct. Both firm conjuncts are preserved, with no added scope.

contract.note: The plain reading treats 'often' as a recurring, documented problem and 'unsolved' as an open research problem. Both are ordinary readings, stretched neither for nor against the speaker.

evidence.note: February 2023 EACL paper: building NLI benchmarks free of shortcut bias is difficult, and leakage persists despite mitigation efforts.
May 2023 experiments find LLMs exploit spurious prompt shortcuts across classification and extraction tasks.
May 2023 review notes some robustness benchmarks have emerged but more curation is needed. This is consistent with an open problem, not a solved one.

reviews.rationale: Research dated within the target period shows shortcut exploitation recurring across tasks and continuing difficulty in building shortcut-free benchmarks. The review's mention of progress does not show the problem was solved. Both parts of the claim meet the support condition.
